title: Apriamo!
subtitle: We're opening!
intro: The keys to the shop in via Marina. Tommaso and the protagonist paint, argue about the name, plan the opening and promise Dora the first ride. Nando predicts rain, Pasquale predicts failure. This unit adds the futuro, the tense of plans, promises and predictions; the indirect object pronouns in full (ti do, le regalo, gli dico); the stressed pronouns (a me, con te, per lui); and the piacere-type verbs (mi serve, ci manca, ti interessa).
objectives: Talk about plans and predictions: [[apriremo il primo marzo]], [[pioverà]], [[fallirete]], [[vedrai]]
Make promises and conditions: [[ti prometto che]], [[se piove, faremo tutto dentro]], [[quando aprirete, verrò]]
Guess with the future: [[sarà Dora]], [[saranno le sette]], [[avrà cinquant'anni]]
Say to whom: [[ti do le chiavi]], [[le regalo il primo giro]], [[gli ho detto di no]], [[a me piace]], [[con te]]
Say what you need and what you miss: [[mi serve una chiave inglese]], [[ci mancano due giorni]], [[ti interessa?]]
canDo: A2 · Spoken production: can talk about plans, intentions and arrangements for the near future.
A2 · Spoken interaction: can make and respond to promises, invitations and predictions; can discuss what to do if or when something happens.
A2 · Listening: can understand a simple weather forecast and a conversation about plans.
A2 · Writing: can write a short announcement or invitation with dates and times.
A2 · Reading: can understand a short notice about opening hours and an invitation.

sections.title: Le chiavi
sections.intro: The first day in the empty shop, and a week before the opening at the bar. Listen for the futuro (apriremo, farò, pioverà, sarà), for the indirect pronouns (ti do, le regalo, gli dico) and for a me, a te.

blocks.title: Ciclofficina Ferrante o Bici & Mare?
blocks.setting: Lunedì mattina, via Marina. Il locale vuoto, lo specchio del barbiere ancora al muro, due secchi di vernice bianca. Tommaso con il rullo; {hero} con le chiavi in mano per la prima volta.

lines.t: Allora. Oggi dipingiamo, domani montiamo il banco, giovedì arrivano gli attrezzi. Apriremo il primo marzo.
lines.n: So. Today we paint, tomorrow we set up the bench, Thursday the tools arrive. We'll open on the first of March.
lines.note: Dipingiamo, montiamo, arrivano: the present for a fixed schedule, like English. Apriremo: the futuro, for the plan further off.

lines.t: Il primo marzo? Ma non abbiamo ancora l'insegna, la partita IVA è di due settimane fa, e non so nemmeno il nome.
lines.n: The first of March? But we don't have the sign yet, the VAT number is two weeks old, and I don't even know the name.
lines.note: Non… nemmeno: not even. Di due settimane fa: two weeks old.

lines.t: Il nome lo sai. Ciclofficina Ferrante. Il tuo cognome è già famoso qui: tuo nonno, tuo bisnonno, le piastrelle di mezzo paese.
lines.n: You know the name. Ciclofficina Ferrante. Your surname is already famous here: your grandfather, your great-grandfather, the tiles of half the town.
lines.note: Il nome lo sai: the noun first, then the pronoun, for emphasis. Ciclofficina: a bike workshop, from ciclo + officina.

lines.t: A me piace Bici & Mare. È più semplice, e i turisti lo capiranno. Ferrante non lo capirà nessuno.
lines.n: I like Bici & Mare. It's simpler, and the tourists will understand it. Nobody will understand Ferrante.
lines.note: A me piace: the stressed pronoun, a me, for contrast (I, unlike you). Capiranno, capirà: futuro of capire.

lines.t: I turisti vengono quattro mesi all'anno. Il paese c'è dodici mesi. E a te, scusa, chi ti ha dato il locale, Dora o un turista?
lines.n: The tourists come four months a year. The town is here twelve months. And you, sorry, who gave you the shop, Dora or a tourist?
lines.note: A te… ti ha dato: stressed and unstressed pronoun together, a very spoken Italian. Dare a qualcuno: ti ha dato = gave to you.

lines.t: Dora. E a Dora regalerò il primo giro, gliel'ho promesso.
lines.n: Dora. And I'll give Dora the first ride, I promised her.
lines.note: Regalerò: futuro. Gliel'ho promesso: glie + l' = to her + it. Unit 14 explains the double pronouns; copy it for now.

lines.t: Allora Ciclofficina Ferrante, e sotto, piccolo: Bici & Mare. Ti va?
lines.n: Then Ciclofficina Ferrante, and underneath, small: Bici & Mare. Does that work for you?
lines.note: Ti va? Literally "does it go to you?": is that OK with you? The most useful indirect pronoun phrase.

lines.t: Mi va. Ma l'insegna la pago io.
lines.n: Works for me. But the sign is on me.
lines.note: Mi va: fine by me. La pago io: I'll pay for it, with io at the end for emphasis.

lines.t: Bene. Adesso dipingi. Ti servono un rullo e una scala. Io farò la parete lunga, tu farai quella corta. Finiremo alle sei, se non parliamo.
lines.n: Good. Now paint. You need a roller and a ladder. I'll do the long wall, you'll do the short one. We'll finish at six, if we don't talk.
lines.note: Ti servono: you need (literally: to you serve). Farò, farai, finiremo: three futures with the short stems. Se non parliamo: se + present is also fine.

lines.t: Parleremo. Ma finiremo lo stesso.
lines.n: We'll talk. But we'll finish anyway.
lines.note: Parleremo: -are verbs change a to e in the future.

notes.phrase: apriremo · farò · farai · finiremo · capiranno · regalerò
notes.note: The futuro: infinitive minus the final -e, plus -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno; -are verbs change the a to e (regalerò); some have short stems (farò).

notes.phrase: ti ha dato · ti servono · ti va? · mi va · gliel'ho promesso
notes.note: Indirect pronouns: to you, to me, to her. Before the verb, like the direct ones.

notes.phrase: A me piace Bici & Mare. · E a te?
notes.note: Stressed pronouns (a me, a te) when you contrast two people or want weight on the person.

notes.phrase: Il nome lo sai. · L'insegna la pago io.
notes.note: Noun first, then its pronoun: spoken emphasis. Recognise it; the neutral order is lo sai, la pago io.

blocks.title: Pioverà
blocks.setting: Una settimana prima dell'apertura. Bar del Corso, ore 18. Nando dietro il banco con il telefono, Pasquale al tavolo con il giornale, Dora in piedi perché «vado via subito» (resterà un'ora).

lines.t: Il primo marzo? Pioverà. Guarda qui: pioggia dal 28 al 3. Sempre così, quando qualcuno apre.
lines.n: The first of March? It'll rain. Look here: rain from the 28th to the 3rd. Always like that, when somebody opens.
lines.note: Pioverà: it will rain. Impersonal, third person.

lines.t: Pioverà, e poi fallirete. Sei mesi, massimo. Un'officina di biciclette in un paese di motorini.
lines.n: It'll rain, and then you'll fail. Six months, maximum. A bicycle workshop in a town of mopeds.
lines.note: Fallirete: voi future of fallire. Pasquale's prediction, delivered as a fact.

lines.t: Pasquale, a te nessuno ha chiesto niente. Diciotto anni fa hai detto la stessa cosa a Nando per il bar.
lines.n: Pasquale, nobody asked you anything. Eighteen years ago you said the same thing to Nando about the bar.
lines.note: A te nessuno ha chiesto: stressed a te at the start for emphasis. Hai detto a Nando: to Nando, with a.

lines.t: E il bar è pieno di gente che non paga. Avevo ragione.
lines.n: And the bar is full of people who don't pay. I was right.
lines.note: Avevo ragione: I was right, imperfetto.

lines.t: Se pioverà, faremo l'inaugurazione dentro. Ci stanno trenta persone, in piedi. Se non pioverà, metteremo le bici sul marciapiede e Dora farà il primo giro fino al porto.
lines.n: If it rains, we'll hold the opening inside. Thirty people fit, standing. If it doesn't rain, we'll put the bikes on the pavement and Dora will do the first ride down to the port.
lines.note: Se pioverà, faremo: Italian puts the future in both halves; English keeps the present after if. Se piove, faremo is also common.

lines.t: Io? In bici? A sessantotto anni? Ti ho detto che ti regalo i biscotti per l'inaugurazione, non che salgo su una bici.
lines.n: Me? On a bike? At sixty-eight? I told you I'm giving you biscuits for the opening, not that I'm getting on a bike.
lines.note: Ti ho detto che ti regalo: told you that I'm giving you. Two ti, two meanings: to you.

lines.t: Me l'hai promesso a giugno, davanti a Chiara. Sarà una bici elettrica: non devi pedalare. Ti piacerà.
lines.n: You promised me in June, in front of Chiara. It'll be an electric bike: you don't have to pedal. You'll like it.
lines.note: Me l'hai promesso: to me + it, two pronouns. Sarà: it will be. Ti piacerà: you'll like it, piacere in the future.

lines.t: Le piacerà. Dora, ti ricordi quando sei salita sul motorino di mio padre nel 1975?
lines.n: She'll like it. Dora, do you remember when you got on my father's moped in 1975?
lines.note: Le piacerà: she'll like it, le = to her.

lines.t: Me lo ricordo. E mi ricordo anche la caviglia. Va bene: un giro, fino al porto, piano. E voi due mi promettete una cosa.
lines.n: I remember. And I also remember the ankle. All right: one ride, to the port, slowly. And you two promise me one thing.
lines.note: Mi promettete: promise me (to me).

lines.t: Dimmi.
lines.n: Tell me.

lines.t: Che quando aprirete, chiuderete all'una e aprirete alle quattro, come tutti. Niente orario continuato. La gente deve mangiare.
lines.n: That when you open, you'll close at one and open at four, like everybody. No continuous hours. People have to eat.
lines.note: Quando aprirete, chiuderete: quando + futuro, futuro. Orario continuato: all-day opening, the enemy of lunch.

lines.t: Te lo prometto. E chi arriverà alle tre troverà il cartello: torno alle quattro.
lines.n: I promise you. And whoever arrives at three will find the sign: back at four.
lines.note: Te lo prometto: to you + it. Chi arriverà troverà: whoever arrives will find.

lines.t: Nessuno arriverà alle tre. Nessuno arriverà e basta.
lines.n: Nobody will arrive at three. Nobody will arrive, full stop.

lines.t: Sarà Don Mimmo a benedire il locale? Chiamalo, se no si offende. E offri da bere: alle undici del mattino la gente ha già fame.
lines.n: Will it be Don Mimmo blessing the shop? Call him, otherwise he'll take offence. And offer drinks: at eleven in the morning people are already hungry.
lines.note: Sarà Don Mimmo a…? Will it be Don Mimmo who…? The priest's blessing: see Living there. Si offende: he gets offended.

notes.phrase: Se pioverà, faremo… · Quando aprirete, chiuderete… · Chi arriverà troverà…
notes.note: After se, quando and chi the future stays in the future in Italian. English says if it rains, when you open, whoever arrives.

notes.phrase: Sarà una bici elettrica. · Ti piacerà. · Le piacerà.
notes.note: Piacere in the future, with ti (to you) and le (to her). The thing liked is the subject, as always.

notes.phrase: me l'hai promesso · te lo prometto · gliel'ho promesso
notes.note: Two pronouns together: mi, ti, gli become me, te, glie before lo. Unit 14; for now, copy the three phrases.
Predictions in the future: the weather, the business, the customers. Only one of them will come true.

questions.q: The shop will be called Bici & Mare, and nothing else.
questions.t: Ciclofficina Ferrante, e sotto, piccolo: Bici & Mare.
questions.why: Ciclofficina Ferrante on top, Bici & Mare underneath, small. A compromise.

questions.q: What does Dora make them promise?
options: To close at one and reopen at four, like everybody.
To give her an electric bike.
questions.why: Chiuderete all'una e aprirete alle quattro, come tutti. Niente orario continuato.

questions.q: Se ___ (piovere), ___ (noi, fare) l'inaugurazione dentro. Dora ___ (fare) il primo giro e Pasquale ___ (dire) che falliremo.
questions.n: If it rains, we'll hold the opening inside. Dora will do the first ride and Pasquale will say we'll fail.

sections.title: L'officina, gli attrezzi, le previsioni
sections.intro: The words of the workshop and the bike, the forecast, and the plans and promises around an opening.

items.n: tool

ex.t: Giovedì arrivano gli attrezzi.
ex.n: The tools arrive on Thursday.

items.note: La cassetta degli attrezzi: the toolbox. Attrezzare: to equip.

items.n: spanner, wrench

ex.t: Mi serve una chiave inglese del dieci.
ex.n: I need a 10 mm spanner.

items.note: Literally "English key". Chiave: key and spanner. Chiave a brugola: Allen key.

items.n: screwdriver

ex.t: Un cacciavite a stella e uno piatto.
ex.n: A Phillips screwdriver and a flat one.

items.note: Invariable plural (caccia + vite, drives the screw). Vite: screw.

items.n: pump

ex.t: Una pompa fuori dal negozio, gratis: così la gente entra.
ex.n: A pump outside the shop, free: that way people come in.

items.note: Gonfiare le gomme: to pump up the tyres.

items.n: chain

ex.t: È saltata la catena. La catena è arrugginita.
ex.n: The chain has come off. The chain is rusty.

items.note: Also the chain of shops and the mountain range.

items.n: brake

ex.t: I freni non tengono. Frenare: to brake.
ex.n: The brakes don't hold.

items.note: Frenare: to brake. Freni a disco: disc brakes.

items.n: wheel

ex.t: La ruota davanti è storta.
ex.n: The front wheel is bent.

items.note: Raggio: spoke. Cerchio: rim. Due ruote: a bike or moped (le due ruote).

items.n: tyre; rubber; chewing gum

ex.t: Ho bucato una gomma. Gomma a terra.
ex.n: I got a puncture. Flat tyre.

items.note: Copertone: the outer tyre; camera d'aria: inner tube. Bucare: to puncture.

items.n: saddle

ex.t: Alza la sella: sei troppo basso.
ex.n: Raise the saddle: you're too low.

items.note: Also a horse's saddle.

items.n: handlebars

ex.t: Il manubrio è largo: è una bici da città.
ex.n: The handlebars are wide: it's a city bike.

items.note: Singular in Italian, plural in English.

items.n: gears; change

ex.t: Il cambio ha ventun marce. Cambia marcia in salita.
ex.n: The gears have twenty-one speeds. Change gear uphill.

items.note: Marcia: a gear (and a march). Cambio also = exchange rate and gearbox.

items.n: padlock, bike lock

ex.t: A Roccamarina nessuno usa il lucchetto. A Lecce sì.
ex.n: In Roccamarina nobody uses a lock. In Lecce they do.

items.n: helmet

ex.t: Il casco non è obbligatorio in bici. Mettilo lo stesso.
ex.n: A helmet isn't compulsory on a bike. Wear it anyway.

items.note: Compulsory on mopeds (motorino) and motorbikes.

items.n: to repair, to fix

ex.t: Ripareremo bici, non motorini. Riparazione in giornata.
ex.n: We'll repair bikes, not mopeds. Same-day repair.

items.note: La riparazione: the repair. Aggiustare: to fix, more colloquial.

items.n: to rent out, to hire

ex.t: D'estate noleggeremo bici ai turisti.
ex.n: In summer we'll rent bikes to tourists.

items.note: Il noleggio: rental. Noleggiare for vehicles; affittare for buildings.

items.n: quote, estimate

ex.t: Le faccio un preventivo: quaranta euro, catena e freni.
ex.n: I'll give you a quote: forty euros, chain and brakes.

items.note: Chiedere / fare un preventivo. See Living there.

items.n: shop sign

ex.t: L'insegna la pago io. Ciclofficina Ferrante.
ex.n: The sign is on me. Ciclofficina Ferrante.

items.note: Insegnare: to teach. Same root: to mark, to show.

items.n: paint

ex.t: Due secchi di vernice bianca. Dipingere: to paint (walls, pictures).
ex.n: Two buckets of white paint.

items.note: Vernice fresca: wet paint. Verniciare: to paint (an object); dipingere: walls and pictures.

items.n: forecast

ex.t: Le previsioni dicono pioggia dal 28 al 3.
ex.n: The forecast says rain from the 28th to the 3rd.

items.note: Previsioni del tempo, always plural. Prevedere: to forecast, to foresee.

items.n: to rain

ex.t: Pioverà. Piove. Ha piovuto / È piovuto tutta la notte.
ex.n: It'll rain. It's raining. It rained all night.

items.note: Impersonal: only third person. Either auxiliary in the past. Nevicare: to snow.

items.n: thunderstorm

ex.t: Un temporale a marzo dura un'ora.
ex.n: A thunderstorm in March lasts an hour.

items.note: Tuono: thunder. Fulmine: lightning. Not "temporary": that is temporaneo.

items.n: clear (sky)

ex.t: Cielo sereno fino a giovedì, poi nuvoloso.
ex.n: Clear skies until Thursday, then cloudy.

items.note: Also calm, serene (a person). Nuvoloso, coperto: cloudy, overcast.

items.n: wind

ex.t: Vento forte da sud: lo scirocco.
ex.n: Strong wind from the south: the sirocco.

items.note: Tira vento: it's windy. Scirocco (hot, from Africa), tramontana (cold, from the north), maestrale.

items.n: degree

ex.t: Domani diciotto gradi. Sabato ventidue.
ex.n: Tomorrow eighteen degrees. Saturday twenty-two.

items.note: Also the degree (university) and the rank.

items.n: humidity

ex.t: L'umidità al porto rovina le catene.
ex.n: The humidity at the port ruins the chains.

items.note: Umido: damp, from unit 10.

items.n: to be nice weather

ex.t: Farà bel tempo? — Farà brutto. Dice Nando.
ex.n: Will the weather be nice? — It'll be bad. Nando says.

items.note: Fa bello / fa brutto: nice / bad weather. Fa caldo / freddo: hot / cold.

items.n: project, plan

ex.t: Il progetto è semplice: riparare, noleggiare, vendere.
ex.n: The plan is simple: repair, rent, sell.

items.note: Avere dei progetti: to have plans. Progettare: to plan, to design.

items.n: intention

ex.t: Ho intenzione di aprire il primo marzo.
ex.n: I intend to open on the first of March.

items.note: Avere intenzione di + infinitive: to intend to. A softer future.

items.n: to promise

ex.t: Ti prometto che chiuderemo all'una. Me l'hai promesso.
ex.n: I promise you we'll close at one. You promised me.

items.note: Promettere a qualcuno di + infinitive, or che + clause. Participle: promesso. La promessa: the promise.

items.n: opening (ceremony)

ex.t: L'inaugurazione è il primo marzo alle undici. Venite tutti.
ex.n: The opening is on the first of March at eleven. Everybody come.

items.note: Inaugurare: to open officially. Apertura: the opening (of hours, of a door).

items.n: to invite

ex.t: Inviteremo tutto il paese. Ti invito a cena.
ex.n: We'll invite the whole town. I'm inviting you to dinner.

items.note: Invitare a + event / infinitive. L'invito: the invitation. Offrire: to treat (I'm paying).

items.n: to bless

ex.t: Don Mimmo benedirà il locale. Benedica!
ex.n: Don Mimmo will bless the shop. Bless you!

items.note: Like dire: benedico, benedirò, benedetto. The priest's job at every opening in the South.

items.n: to hope

ex.t: Spero che non piova. Speriamo bene!
ex.n: I hope it doesn't rain. Let's hope for the best!

items.note: Sperare di + infinitive (same subject), sperare che + subjunctive (unit 16). Speriamo! = fingers crossed.

items.n: to manage, to succeed

ex.t: Riusciremo ad aprire in tempo? — Ci riusciremo.
ex.n: Will we manage to open in time? — We'll manage.

items.note: Riuscire a + infinitive. Like uscire: riesco, riuscirò. Essere in the past: sono riuscito / a.

items.n: to fail, to go bankrupt

ex.t: Fallirete in sei mesi, dice Pasquale.
ex.n: You'll fail in six months, says Pasquale.
ex.note: -isc- verb: fallisco. Il fallimento: failure, bankruptcy.

items.n: opening hours

ex.t: Orario: 9–13 e 16–20. Lunedì chiuso.
ex.n: Hours: 9–1 and 4–8. Closed Mondays.

items.note: Orario continuato: all day without a break. Orario spezzato: with the lunch break. See Living there.

items.n: customer, client

ex.t: Il primo cliente avrà la riparazione gratis.
ex.n: The first customer will get a free repair.

items.note: Same form for men and women; only the article changes.

sections.title: Apriremo, pioverà, ti prometto
sections.intro: Five pieces: the forms of the futuro, its uses with se and quando and for guessing, the indirect object pronouns, the stressed pronouns, and the piacere-type verbs. Reference pages at the end of each block.

blocks.title: Futuro semplice: the forms
blocks.rule: Drop the final -e of the infinitive and add -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno; -are verbs change the a to e (parlare → parlerò). Spelling: -care / -gare keep the hard sound with h (cercherò, pagherò); -ciare / -giare drop the i (comincerò, mangerò). Short stems: sarò, avrò, andrò, farò, darò, starò, vedrò, vivrò, saprò, potrò, dovrò, verrò, vorrò, rimarrò, berrò, terrò. Stress on the ending: parlerÒ, parlerÀ, parleRANno.

blocks.caption: [[aprire|to open]], [[essere|to be]], [[fare|to do]] · futuro semplice
blocks.note: Aprire is regular (aprirò); essere and fare have short stems (sarò, farò).

items.t: Apriremo il primo marzo. Io farò la parete lunga, tu farai quella corta, e finiremo alle sei.
items.n: We'll open on the first of March. I'll do the long wall, you'll do the short one, and we'll finish at six.

items.t: Pagherò l'insegna, cercherò un'altra scala e comincerò domani.
items.n: I'll pay for the sign, look for another ladder and start tomorrow.

items.t: Verranno tutti, berranno tutto e non rimarrà niente.
items.n: Everybody will come, they'll drink everything and nothing will be left.

items.t: Sarò stanco, ma sarò contento. Avremo un'officina.
items.n: I'll be tired, but I'll be happy. We'll have a workshop.

items.why: -are verbs change a to e.
Spelling: keep the hard c / g with h; drop the i after ci / gi.
Short stems.
Essere is sarò; fare, dare, stare keep the a.
Stress on the ending.

blocks.title: What the future is for: plans, predictions, guesses, se and quando
blocks.rule: Plans and intentions further off (apriremo a marzo), predictions (pioverà, fallirete), promises (ti chiamerò), and guesses about the present (sarà Dora = it must be Dora; saranno le sette = it's probably seven). After se, quando, appena, finché with a future main clause, Italian keeps the future in the subordinate too (quando aprirete, verrò), where English uses the present. For the near future, the present is more common: domani dipingiamo.

head: Use
Italian
English
rows: Apriremo il primo marzo. Noleggeremo bici d'estate.
We'll open on 1 March. We'll rent bikes in summer.
Pioverà. Fallirete in sei mesi. Vedrai.
It'll rain. You'll fail in six months. You'll see.
Ti chiamerò. Chiuderemo all'una, te lo prometto.
I'll call you. We'll close at one, I promise.
Sarà Dora. Saranno le sette. Avrà cinquant'anni. Dove sarà Tommaso?
It must be Dora. It must be about seven. He must be fifty. Where can Tommaso be?
If it rains, we'll do everything inside.
Quando aprirete, verrò. Appena arriverà, gli dirò tutto.
When you open, I'll come. As soon as he arrives, I'll tell him everything.
Chi arriverà alle tre troverà il cartello. Resterò finché avrò soldi.
Whoever arrives at three will find the sign. I'll stay as long as I have money.
Domani dipingiamo. Giovedì arrivano gli attrezzi. Stasera ti chiamo.
Tomorrow we're painting. Thursday the tools arrive. I'll call you tonight.

blocks.title: If it rains / se pioverà
blocks.text: English refuses the future after *if* and *when*: *if it rains, we'll…*. Italian allows it and, when the main clause is in the future, prefers it: [[se pioverà, faremo tutto dentro]], [[quando aprirete, verrò]]. [[Se piove, faremo…]] is also fine and common in speech. What you cannot do is the English pattern with the present in the main clause: [[quando aprite, vengo]] means something more casual, almost a habit.

items.t: Chi sarà a quest'ora? — Sarà Dora con i biscotti.
items.n: Who can it be at this hour? — It must be Dora with the biscuits.

items.t: Quando avremo l'insegna, faremo le foto. Appena le faremo, le metteremo online.
items.n: When we have the sign, we'll take photos. As soon as we take them, we'll put them online.

items.t: Se non pioverà, Dora farà il primo giro; se pioverà, lo farà la settimana dopo.

blocks.title: Indirect object pronouns: ti do, le regalo, gli dico
blocks.rule: Mi, ti, gli (to him), le (to her), Le (to you, formal), ci, vi, gli (to them; loro after the verb in formal style) replace a + person. They go before the conjugated verb, attach to infinitives and tu / noi / voi imperatives, and do not make the participle agree. The verbs that take them: dare, dire, regalare, promettere, chiedere, telefonare, scrivere, mandare, rispondere, piacere, servire, mancare, sembrare, interessare, bastare.

blocks.title: Stressed pronouns: a me, con te, per lui
blocks.rule: Me, te, lui, lei, Lei, noi, voi, loro are the pronouns used after prepositions (con te, per lui, da noi, senza di me) and for emphasis or contrast (a me piace, non a te). As direct objects, after the verb, they stress the person: cerco te, non lui. They replace the unstressed pronoun when you want weight on the person; they never double it except in colloquial a me mi.

blocks.title: Mi serve, ci mancano, ti interessa: the piacere family
blocks.rule: Servire (to be needed), mancare (to be missing, to be missed), interessare, bastare (to be enough), sembrare, dispiacere, succedere and piacere all work the same way: the thing is the subject, the person an indirect pronoun. sections.title: Parlo, parlò, parlerò: the stress that changes the tense
sections.intro: In the future the stress sits on the ending, and the written accent on -ò and -à is there to prove it. Move the stress and you change the tense: pàrlo (I speak), parlò (he spoke, passato remoto), parlerò (I will speak). This section is about hearing and saying that difference.

blocks.caption: Three tenses, three stresses
head: Present
Passato remoto (unit 17)
Futuro
blocks.note: Io present: stress on the stem. Lui passato remoto: stress on the last syllable, written. Io futuro: stress on the -rò, written. The accent marks are not optional.

pairs.tip: PAR-lo versus par-LÒ. The written accent on the o.

SA-ra the person, sa-RÀ the future.
From unit 8: the same letters, two stresses.
Both on the ending. The loro form is stressed on the penultimate: faRANno, never on the final o.

head: Person
Say it
blocks.note: Every form is stressed on the syllable with the r, or just after it. Never on the stem: a-PRI-rò is wrong.

blocks.title: Write the accent, say the accent
blocks.text: The exercises accept [[faro]] for [[farò]] as "almost right"; a shop sign, a message to Dora, a contract do not. Type the ò and the à. And when you speak, lean on the last syllable so hard it almost breaks: [[apriremo il primo MARzo, pioveRÀ, falliRETE]]. The south stresses the future like a threat. Pasquale certainly does.

sections.title: L'inaugurazione, l'orario, la bici
sections.intro: The priest and the ribbon, the hours a shop keeps and the weeks it closes, bicycles in a country of mopeds, and how to ask for a quote without offending anyone.

blocks.text: A shop in a southern town does not just open: it is [[inaugurato]]. The owner picks a Saturday, prints an invitation ([[siete tutti invitati]]) and tapes it to the bar's door, and at eleven in the morning the street fills up. There is a ribbon to cut, there are flowers from the other shopkeepers with a ribbon reading [[auguri]], and there is the parish priest, [[Don Mimmo]] in Roccamarina, who sprinkles holy water on the walls, the tools and the owner, says a short prayer and stays for the prosecco. Nobody is very religious; everybody expects the blessing, and skipping it is a statement you do not want to make in your first week. Then: [[rustici]], [[pasticciotti]], [[taralli]], prosecco and spumante in plastic cups, the mayor if he has nothing else, the band if you are the pharmacy, and a photo for the local Facebook group. By one o'clock everyone has gone to lunch, which is the point of the next paragraph.

Italian shops keep the [[orario spezzato]]: open from about 9 to 1, closed for lunch, open again from about 4 to 8 (later in summer in the South). The [[orario continuato]], all day without a break, is for supermarkets, malls and the big cities; in a town like Roccamarina it marks you as a chain or a stranger, and Dora is not alone in thinking it uncivilised. Add the [[giorno di chiusura]], a weekly closing day (Monday for hairdressers and many shops, Thursday afternoon for some, Sunday for nearly all), and the [[chiusura per ferie]]: two or three weeks in August when the sign says [[chiuso per ferie, riapriamo il 26]] and the town is run by the bars. A bike shop at the seaside inverts the logic: open seven days from June to September, closed on Mondays and half of January. Whatever you choose, print it on the door, and expect people to knock anyway.

blocks.title: Chiedere un preventivo
blocks.text: For any job, from a chain to a kitchen, you ask [[mi fa un preventivo?]] (will you give me a quote?) and you get a figure, usually spoken, sometimes written, almost never final. It is not rude to ask; it is rude to accept the first one without a small face of doubt. [[Quanto mi viene?]] (how much will it come to?) and [[tutto compreso?]] (all included?) are the two follow-ups. For the workshop, the protagonist will give quotes by the job ([[catena e freni, quaranta euro]]) and learn that in a small town the quote is also a conversation about the customer's cousin's bike.
La bici in un paese di motorini

Italy worships cycling as a sport, the [[Giro d'Italia]] in May and the names of Coppi and Pantani, and neglects it as transport, especially in the South, where the [[motorino]] (moped) is the vehicle of every teenager and the car of every adult. Cycle paths ([[piste ciclabili]]) exist in the North and along some coasts; in Puglia the [[Ciclovia Adriatica]] is slowly being built, and the flat Salento with its small roads is one of the best places in Italy to ride, which the tourists have noticed before the locals. The town's own bikes are old, heavy, unlocked and loved; the tourists' are rented. Pasquale's prediction, [[un'officina di biciclette in un paese di motorini]], is half right: the locals bring mopeds, and Tommaso fixes them anyway. The e-bike boom since 2020 is the other half: Dora's first ride will be electric, and so will most of the sales.

blocks.title: Nando's forecast
blocks.text: Every town has a Nando: the bar owner who reads three weather apps and announces rain for any public event, and a Pasquale who announces failure. Both are wrong most of the time and right often enough to keep their reputations. The correct response to either is [[speriamo bene]] (let's hope for the best), a shrug, and inviting them anyway. On the first of March it will rain until ten, stop at a quarter to eleven, and Nando will say he predicted exactly that.
